5202:
** ὑδρο-ποτέω**,
**drink water,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.71, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 6.2.26, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 561c, 4th c.BC: Ephorus Historicus (?) in “PLit.Lond.” 114, NT.1Tim.5.23, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.117, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.13.21.}}—**ὑδροπωτέω** is the more correct form _accusative_ to {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Ammonius Grammaticus “περὶ ὁμοίων καὶ διαφόρων λέξεων” p.111 V.}}
5203:
** ὑδρωπ-ικός**, ή, όν,
**suffering from dropsy,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 6.27, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 871b24, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 13.2.2, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.103, NT.Luke.14.2, “POxy.” 1088.63 (1st c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.63: _metaphorically_, ναῦς ὑ. “Anthologia Graeca” 11.332 (1st c.AD: Nicarchus Epigrammaticus).}}
5206:
** υἱο-θεσία**, ἡ,
**adoption as a son,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus 130.18 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus}}; in a religious sense, πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας {{NT|NT.Rom.8.15, compare 23, NT.Gal.4.5}}; frequently in Inscrr., in the phrase καθ᾽ υἱοθεσίαν, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“GDI” 2581.218 (Delph., 2nd c.BC), “SIG” 581.102 (Crete, 2nd c.BC, ὑο-): _plural_, νεανίσκων υἱοθεσίας ποιεῖσθαι 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 4.53.}}
5215:
** ὕμνος**, ὁ,
**hymn, ode, in praise** of gods or heroes (καί τι ἦν εἶδος ῳδῆς εὐχαὶ πρὸς θεούς, ὄνομα δὲ ὕμνοι ἐπεκαλοῦντο {{Refs 8th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 700b; ὕμνους θεοῖς καὶ ἐγκώμια τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς [prev. author] “R.” 607a, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1448b27), once in 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ἀοιδῆς ὕμνος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.429 (followed by Demodocus' song of the Wooden Horse, 499ff)}}; ὕμνῳ νικήσαντα φέρειν τρίποδ᾽ {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 657; ἀνδρῶν τε παλαιῶν ἠδὲ γυναικῶν ὕμνον ἀείδουσιν “hymnus ad Apollinem” 161; frequently in 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus, ὕμνος πολύφατος, ἐπικώμιος, etc., “O.” 1.8, “N.” 8.50, +others; Θήρωνος Ὀλυμπιονίκαν ὕμνον “O.” 3.3; and in 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, ὑφάνας ὕμνον 5.10, compare 6.11, +others}}; ὕμνοι θεῶν **to** or **in honour of** the gods, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 801d; τιμῶν θεὰν ὕμνοισιν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hippolytus” 56; τοὺς χοροὺς.. καὶ τοὺς ὕ. τῷ θεῷ ποιεῖτε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.51, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 177a}}; ὕμνοι Δαυείδ **psalms** of {{NT+6th c.AD+|6th c.AD: David Philosophus, LXX.2Ch.7.6; ψαλμοὶ καὶ ὕ. καὶ ᾠδαί NT.Eph.5.19}}: in Trag. also of **mournful songs,** addressed to gods or heroes, τὸν δυσκέλαδον ὕ. Ἐρινύος {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 868 (Lyric poetry), compare “Pers.” 620, 625 (_anapaest meter_), “Ch.” 475 (Lyric poetry); ὕ. ἐξ Ἐρινύων, δέσμιος φρενῶν, ἀφόρμικτος [prev. author] “Eu.” 331 (Lyric poetry), compare 306; ἐν ἀλύροις κλέοντες ὕμνοις 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 447 (Lyric poetry)}}; ὕ. Ἅιδου, of one whose songs are death, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista Comedy texts 69 (Lyric poetry).}} —On ὕμνοι of various kinds see Men.Rh.p.333 {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; ὁ κυρίως ὕ. πρὸς κιθάραν ᾔδετο ἑστώτων 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Chr.” cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.320 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, compare 1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus cited in “Etymologicum Magnum” 777.9}}. [Most commonly ῡ, but only by position; ῠ proved by εὔῠμνος (which see), ῠμνῳδεῖ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 990 (Lyric poetry), ῠμνήσω 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 72 (Lyric poetry).]}}
5218:
** ὑπᾰκοή**, ἡ,
(ὑπακούω) **obedience,** {{NT+6th c.AD+|NT.Rom.5.19, “PMasp.” 159.24 (6th c.AD)}}; **answer to prayer,** {{LXX|LXX.2Ki.22.36.}}
5230:
** ὑπέρακμος**, ον,
**sexually well-developed,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.1Cor.7.36, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.22}}; = Latin _exoletus,_ {{Refs|“Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”}}: _neuter_ _plural_ as _adverb_, ἀκολασταίνοντες ὑ. {{Refs|12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1915.20.}}
5239:
** ὑπερεκ-τείνω**,
**stretch out beyond measure,** ἑαυτούς {{NT|NT.2Cor.10.14}}:—_passive_, **stretch out beyond,** {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus “Inst.” 59, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 284}}; πόλλ᾽ ὑπερεξετάθης conjecture for πουλὺ παρεξ- in {{Refs 6th c.AD+|“Anthologia Graeca” 9.643 (6th c.AD: Agathias Historicus et Epigrammaticus).}}
5240:
Included with: ** ὑπερεκ-χέω**,
**pour out over,** _metaphorically_, εἰς τὴν ἐπαρχίαν τὰς τιμάς {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 1.21.4}}:—_passive_, **overflow,** {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.Joel.2.24, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 11.89, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.362, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “De Natura Animalium - Ar.Byzantine Epit.” 12.41, etc.}}:—also **ὑπερεκ-χύνομαι** in {{NT|NT.Luke.6.38}}; _future_ -χυθήσομαι variant in {{LXX|LXX.Joel.2.24.}}
5243:
** ὑπερηφᾰν-ία**, ἡ,
**arrogance,** {{NT+6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Solon Lyricus cited in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 5.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 219c, 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Characteres” 24, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 252, Aristeas 262, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ κακιῶν ί” p.16 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, +others, NT.Mark.7.22; ὑ. τοῦ τρόπου 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 5.2.27; τοῦ βίου 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.137}}: also with _genitive_ objecti, **contempt towards** or **for**.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 391c, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.195 ([πάντων ἀνθρώπων] secl. Blass).}}
5245:
** ὑπερνῑκάω**,
**prevail completely over,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἑβδομάδων - Die Hippokratische Schrift von der Siebenzahl” 50, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 19.645}}; **to be more than conqueror,** {{NT+4th c.AD+|NT.Rom.8.37: with _accusative_, τὰς Χάριτας, μίμημα, 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Descriptiones” 30.9, 4.}}
5248:
** ὑπερπερισσ-εύω**,
**abound much more, be in great excess,** χάρις {{NT|NT.Rom.5.20}}:—_middle_, ὑ. τῇ χαρᾷ {{NT|NT.2Cor.7.4.}}
5250:
** ὑπερπλεονάζω**,
**abound exceedingly,** {{NT+2nd c.BC+|NT.1Tim.1.14, Vett. Val. 85.17; ὁ -άζων ἀήρ 2nd-1st c.BC(?): Hero Mechanicus “(Spiritalia) Pneumatica” 1.10.}}
5266:
** ὑπόδημ-α**, ατος, τό,
(ὑποδέω) **sole bound under the foot with straps, sandal,** ποσὶν.. ὑποδήματα δοῦσα {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.369; ποσὶν.. ὑποδήματα δοίην 18.361, compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.195, etc.; ποδὸς ὑ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.128a, etc.}}; whereas ὑπόδημα κοῖλον is a **shoe** or **half-boot,** which covered the whole foot (see. κοῖλος 1.1); ὑπόδημα is sometimes used alone in this sense,{{Refs 5th c.BC+|compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 983 (and Scholia (at [prev. work])), 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1392a32}}; εἰς ὑποδήματα γράφειν put down as paid for **shoes,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 32.20 (_passive_)}}; δεξιὸν εἰς ὑ., ἀριστερὸν εἰς ποδάνιπτρα, of one who is ready for anything, perhaps alluding to Theramenes (see. κόθορνος 3){{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 914 (perhaps 3rd-2nd c.BC: Aristophanes Byzantinus Philosophus, compare 1st c.BC: Didymus Grammaticus and 2nd c.BC: Polemo Historicus (“fragment” 101 M.) cited in 2nd c.AD(?): Helladius Epigrammaticus cited in 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc. “Bibliotheca - Patrologia Graeca” p.533 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus)}}; similar words are ascribed to {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Pythagoras Philosophus by 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 21}}.ιά (where ὑπόδησις is used); τὸ ὑ. ἔρραψας μὲν σύ, ὑπεδήσατο δὲ Ἀρισταγόρης {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.1, compare 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Epistulae” 52; ὁ σπάρτος, ἐξ οὗ πλέκουσιν ὑποδήματα τοῖς ὑποζυγίοις 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.502.}}
5267:
** ὑπόδῐκος**, ον,
(δίκη) **brought to trial** or **liable to be tried,** Legal cited in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 10.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 954a, +others, “PHal.” 1.72, +others (3rd c.BC)}}; οὐχ ὑ. [ἐστι] τὰ εἰκότα not **liable to action,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1376a22}}; τινος **for** a thing, ὑ. γενέσθαι χερῶν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 260 (Lyric poetry); ἀνδραποδισμοῦ 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 879a; οὐδενὸς τούτων 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.31; τῆς κακώσεως 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.32 (ἐπίδ- codices)}}; φόνου {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 54.25; τοῦ βλάβους “PHal.” 1.101 (3rd c.BC): with the person injured in _dative_, ὑ. τῷ παθόντι Legal cited in 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.10; ὑ. τῷ ἐθέλοντι τιμωρεῖν γιγνέσθω 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 871b}}; τῶν διπλασίων ὑ. ἔστω τῷ βλαφθέντι let him be **liable to forfeit** twice the amount to the person damaged,{{Refs 1st c.BC+|[prev. work] 846b (but ὑ. ποτὶ διπλοῦν “IG” 5(1).1390.78 (Andania, 1st c.BC))}}; ὑ. ἀσεβείας γιγνέσθω τῷ ἐθέλοντι {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 868d; ἵνα ὑ. γένηται πᾶς ὁ κόσμος τῷ θεῷ NT.Rom.3.19.}}
5269:
** ὑποζώννῡμι**
(_infinitive_ ὑποζωνύναι in {{Refs|“IG” 12.73.9)}} and **ὑποζωννύω** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 27.3.3}}, **undergird,** τοὺς ἵππους ῥυτῆρσι {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Eumenes” 11; ὑ. τινὰ τοῖς ποσσίν “Anthologia Graeca” 12.222 (2nd c.AD: Strato Epigrammaticus)}}; ὁ ὑπεζωκὼς τὰς πλευράς (i.e. ὑμήν), or _absolutely_ ὁ ὑπεζωκώς, **the pleura,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Alexander Aphrodisiensis Philosophus “Problemata - Physici et Medici Graeci Minores” 1.53, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 2.591 (ὑμήν}} is expressed in {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|Diocl.fragment 64, 2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 44.23.45, Oracle texts Chald. cited in 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 265)}}; ὑπεζωκότες foetal **membranes,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.58}}; **lining** of the intestines, {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus “fragment” 58:}} —_passive_, especially in _perfect_ _participle_, ζειρὰς ὑπεζωμένοι (variant {-ζωσμ-}) **girt** with ζειραί (which see), {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.69; ὑπεζωσμένοι ἱμάντας 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Romulus” 26: _absolutely_, ὑπεζωμέναι}} (οι) **girt up,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.85 (with variants):}} —especially,
**II** **brace** a ship, so as to make her seaworthy {{NT+2nd c.BC+|compare (ὑπόζωμα 11), “IG” [same place], 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus [same place], NT.Act.27.17; ὑπέζωται “IG” 22.1621.68.}}
**III** ὑπεζῶσθαι· τὸ εἰς ἄνδρας ἐλθεῖν, Φιλητᾶς, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}} (probably = **come to man's estate**).
5276:
** ὑπολήνιον**, τό,
**vessel placed under a press** to receive the wine or oil, **vat,** {{LXX+NT+2nd c.AD+|LXX.Joel.3(4).13, LXX.Isa.16.10, NT.Mark.12.1, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 10.130; uncertain meaning in “POxy.” 1735.5 (4th c.AD): as}} _adjective_, κρατῆρας -ίους uncertain meaning in {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“OGI” 383.147 (Commagene, 1st c.BC).}}
5286:
** ὑποπόδ-ιον**, τό,
**footstool,** {{LXX+4th c.BC+|Inscriptiones Graecae 22.1394.15 (4th c.BC), 4th c.BC: Chares Historicus 2 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus, “Schwyzer” 200 (Crete, 2nd c.BC), “PTeb.” 45.38 (2nd c.BC), LXX.Psa.98(99).5, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hist.Conscr.” 27, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.68, Scholia Callias Epigrammaticus in Διηγήσεις vii 29.}}
